aves.description: Individual bird weighing, flock uniformity and comparison against breed standard targets.

huevos.description: Egg weight sampling, distribution analysis and automatic grading into size categories.

generico.description: Statistical analysis of any quantitative variable, with real or experimental data, for teaching and practice.
generico.sameEngine: It uses the same verified statistical engine as the bird and egg modules, so a classroom exercise and a production analysis are solved with the same tools.

criterion.label: Uniformity criterion (band around the mean)
criterion.note: Uniformity is the % of birds within mean ±{pct}%. It is a descriptive band, not a confidence interval.

descriptive.standardized: Standardized index vs. target: {z} standard deviations

histogram.caption: Weight (g) — {modo}, {clases} bins ({regla})

tTest.targetUnavailable: Target weight (enter line and age first)
tTest.needMu0: Enter the hypothesized mean μ₀ to run the test.
tTest.cannotRun: The test cannot be run: at least 2 weights with variability (SD > 0) are required.
tTest.rejectText: At a significance level of {alpha}, there is statistical evidence that the flock's mean weight {dir} {mu0}. The observed difference is {diff} g ({pct}%).
tTest.notRejectText: At a significance level of {alpha}, no sufficient statistical evidence was found to conclude that the flock's mean weight {dir} {mu0}. This does NOT prove the means are equal: only that the data do not allow the difference to be asserted.
tTest.warnVerySmall: • Very small sample (n={n} < 10): the test has low power and depends heavily on normality.
tTest.warnSmall: • Small sample (n={n} < 30): check normality in the diagnostics tab before trusting the result.
tTest.warnSkew: • Markedly skewed distribution: the p-value may not be reliable with this sample.
tTest.warnOutliers: • {n} possible outlier(s) that may influence the result (see the Outliers tab).
tTest.warnIndependence: • The test assumes independent observations and representative (ideally random) sampling.
tTest.svgAlt: Critical region of the t-test with {df} degrees of freedom and the observed statistic t={t}

diagnostics.needFour: At least 4 weights are needed for the distribution diagnostics.
diagnostics.boxplotAlt: Box plot: median {mediana} g, quartiles {q1} and {q3} g, {atipicos} outliers
diagnostics.boxplotCaption: Weight (g) — box: Q1–Q3, line: median, blue dot: mean, red circles: outliers
diagnostics.qqAlt: Normal Q-Q plot: points close to the diagonal indicate compatibility with the normal distribution
diagnostics.normalNotRejected: The normality hypothesis is not rejected (p ≥ 0.05): the data are compatible with a normal distribution. This does not prove they are normal.
diagnostics.normalRejected: The normality hypothesis is rejected (p < 0.05): the data show departures from normality. Check the histogram and the Q-Q plot to understand what kind.
diagnostics.testsDisagree: ⚠️ The two tests disagree at 5%: borderline evidence. Give priority to inspecting the histogram and the Q-Q plot.
diagnostics.k2Unreliable: ⚠️ With n < 20 the K² test is unreliable; give priority to graphical inspection.
diagnostics.normalityCaveat: A normality test does not replace graphical inspection; and in large samples, small and irrelevant departures can yield a significant p.
diagnostics.normalityNeedMore: At least 3 weights with variability are required for Shapiro-Wilk (and 8 for D'Agostino-Pearson).
diagnostics.skewMarkedRight: Marked skewness (G1 = {g1}): the right tail (heavy birds) is longer.
diagnostics.skewMarkedLeft: Marked skewness (G1 = {g1}): the left tail (light birds) is longer.
diagnostics.heavyTails: Tails heavier than the normal (G2 = {g2}): there are more extreme birds than expected.
diagnostics.noOutliers: No weight flagged by the 1.5×IQR, 3×IQR, |Z|>3 or modified-Z (MAD) rules.
diagnostics.outlierCaveat: A flagged value is not necessarily an error: it may be a genuinely small or large bird. Check whether it was a weighing or typing error before deciding. Excluding here is temporary and only for comparison; it does not delete the data.

ai.title: Assistant and interpretation
ai.localIntro: Step-by-step explanation generated locally from the computed results — it always works, with no external services.
ai.onlySpanish: The explanatory content of the academic mode is available in Spanish only.
ai.aiIntro: The assistant receives the already computed results (it never calculates on its own) and writes an interpretation together with its limitations. It requires an API key; if none is available, the application still works with the local academic mode.
ai.noServer: The server could not be reached.
ai.disclaimer: Text generated by AI from locally computed results. It does not replace professional judgement.

spc.notYetTitle: A control chart is not yet appropriate for this flock.
spc.notYetBody: There are {n} valid weigh-in(s) and at least {min} are required to estimate minimally reliable control limits (ideally 20+). With few subgroups the limits become so uncertain that they would produce false alarms or give false reassurance.
spc.notYetHint: In the meantime, the Trend tab shows how weight, CV and uniformity evolve, which is the correct reading with few weigh-ins.
spc.whyNotXbar: Raw mean weight is not charted: in growing birds the mean rises naturally and an X̄ chart would flag that trend as "out of control". What is monitored are quantities that stay approximately stable between weigh-ins: CV, uniformity and % deviation from the breed standard target. Each weigh-in is treated as an individual observation (I-MR chart).
spc.rule1: • Nelson rule 1: point {punto} outside the control limits ({valor}).
spc.rule2Above: • Nelson rule 2: nine consecutive points above the centre line (up to point {punto}).
spc.rule2Below: • Nelson rule 2: nine consecutive points below the centre line (up to point {punto}).
spc.rule3Up: • Nelson rule 3: six consecutive points steadily rising (up to point {punto}).
spc.rule3Down: • Nelson rule 3: six consecutive points steadily falling (up to point {punto}).
spc.signalNote: A signal indicates non-random variation worth investigating (feed, environment, health, weighing error); on its own it is not a diagnosis.
spc.noSignals: No signals from Nelson rules 1-3: the variation in {serie} between weigh-ins is compatible with random variation.
